titel: Long-term care and health insurance in old age
kurz: What a place in a care home costs, why two pensioners with the same portfolio pay different contributions, and when the social assistance authority can claim the children's income and gifts.

bloecke.md:
In 2015, the social long-term care insurance (soziale Pflegeversicherung) counted around 2.8 million people in need of care; in 2025 there were 6.0 million. Over the same period, its expenditure rose from €29.0 billion to €73.8 billion, by 8.2% in 2025 alone. Part of the increase is due to demographic change, another part to the broader definition of the need for care introduced in 2017, which puts cognitive impairments on an equal footing with physical ones.

Two things follow from this for your own planning. The need for care affects many people, and financing it is not getting any cheaper. The contribution rate for the social long-term care insurance was 2.35% in 2016 and 3.6% in 2026, or 4.2% for childless persons aged 23 and over (Section 55 SGB XI, Social Code Book XI, long-term care insurance).

bloecke.titel: Expenditure of the social long-term care insurance 2015-2025
bloecke.unter: Expenditure has more than doubled in ten years, and the insured bear the higher costs through the contribution rate and the co-payment.

bloecke.md:
## Classification into care levels

The amount of the benefit depends on the remaining independence and not on the diagnosis. For this purpose, the Medical Service (Medizinischer Dienst) assesses six modules and weights the results into a score. The modules are mobility, cognitive and communicative abilities, behaviour and psychological problems, self-care, coping with illness- and therapy-related demands, and organisation of everyday life. A person with dementia who can still walk can therefore reach the same [[Care level (Pflegegrad)|care level (Pflegegrad)]] as a person after a stroke.

bloecke.titel: Care levels and benefits from the long-term care insurance fund for full inpatient care (Section 43 SGB XI)

bloecke.md:
These amounts have applied since 1 January 2025. Section 30 SGB XI provides for the next adjustment on 1 January 2028. More important than their level is the fact that they are **fixed amounts**. The fund pays the amount set out in the law, regardless of what the care home charges.

## Co-payment and care home supplement

The residents bear the rest as a co-payment (Eigenanteil). On 1 July 2026, the national average consisted of three items: the uniform care home co-payment (einrichtungseinheitlicher Eigenanteil) of €2,088, €1,068 for accommodation and meals and €521 in investment costs. Together that is €3,677 a month. The uniform care home co-payment includes a training levy (Ausbildungsumlage) of around €150. The amounts differ considerably between the federal states, ranging from €3,190 in Saxony-Anhalt to €4,105 in Bremen.

*Uniform* (einrichtungseinheitlich) means that this item is the same for care levels 2 to 5 within a care home. With a higher care level, the fund pays more, but the bill for the resident does not rise. Only this item is reduced by the [[Care home supplement (Leistungszuschlag)|care home supplement (Leistungszuschlag)]] under Section 43c SGB XI. The supplement is graded according to the length of stay and amounts to 15% in the first year, 30% from the 13th month, 50% from the 25th and 75% from the 37th month. It does not reduce accommodation, meals or investment costs.

bloecke.titel: Co-payment in a care home by length of stay, national average 1 Jul 2026
bloecke.unter: The care home supplement only reduces the lower section of the bars, the care-related co-payment. The €1,589 for accommodation, meals and investment costs stays the same. The training levy is included in the care-related co-payment.

bloecke.titel: Four years in a care home at the national average
bloecke.md:
- Months 1-12: €3,364 × 12 = €40,368
- Months 13-24: €3,051 × 12 = €36,612
- Months 25-36: €2,633 × 12 = €31,596
- Months 37-48: €2,111 × 12 = €25,332
- Total: €133,908

A net pension of €1,600 covers €76,800 over these 48 months. The remaining €57,108 has to come from assets or from assistance with care costs (Hilfe zur Pflege) under SGB XII (Social Code Book XII, social assistance).

bloecke.titel: Cumulative funding gap with a net pension of €1,600 (illustrative calculation)
bloecke.unter: The gap grows by a smaller amount each year. The care home supplement only provides substantial relief once most of the capital has already been used up.

bloecke.md: With the move into a care home, rent, service charges and spending on food fall away. The item for accommodation and meals therefore partly replaces expenses that were incurred anyway before. A calculation that does not offset the previous household costs considerably overestimates the capital requirement. However, the vast majority of people in need of care are looked after at home, mostly by relatives. There the financial gap is smaller, but the caring relatives lose paid work. This loss of income does not appear in any care statistics and mainly affects women between 50 and 65.

## Supplementary long-term care insurance

A long-term care daily allowance policy (Pflegetagegeldversicherung) pays an agreed amount once a care level has been determined, regardless of what the care costs in the individual case and where it takes place. This is its advantage over policies that only reimburse bills. Its disadvantage is the long term, because the adjustable premiums may have to remain affordable for forty years. If the policy is surrendered at 78 because the premium is no longer affordable, all payments are lost, because the ageing reserve (Alterungsrückstellung) remains with the insurer. Based on studies by Stiftung Warentest, Finanztip quoted around €60 a month for a policy taken out at 45 and around €90 for a policy taken out at 55. These figures date from 2022 and are likely to be higher today. The state-subsidised Pflege-Bahr, with an allowance of €5 a month, does without a health assessment, but offers only low benefits and has waiting periods.

A second disadvantage is the lack of indexation. A daily allowance amounting to €1,800 a month that becomes payable in 25 years has the purchasing power of only around €1,100 at 2% inflation. The co-payment rises with care home costs during this time. Indexation options offset this, but increase the premium.

punkte: Also covers an early need for care if no capital has yet been saved at 55
Fixed daily allowance regardless of the costs incurred and of where care takes place
The money is earmarked and cannot be spent on other things beforehand
Pflege-Bahr without a health assessment, so also accessible with pre-existing conditions
Premium increases can make the contract unaffordable after 30 years
On surrender, everything paid in is lost; there is no surrender value
Without indexation, the benefit loses a third or more in real terms
Saved capital can be used even without an established care level and can be inherited

bloecke.md:
## Health insurance in retirement

Two retired women with the same assets can pay different contributions solely because of their insurance history. The decisive factor is the prior insurance period (Vorversicherungszeit) under Section 5(1) no. 11 SGB V (Social Code Book V, health insurance). Pensioners who had statutory insurance for nine tenths of the second half of their working life are compulsorily insured in the [[Health insurance for pensioners (KVdR)|health insurance for pensioners (KVdR)]]. Compulsory insurance, voluntary insurance and family insurance count equally here. All that matters is that it was a statutory fund.

Compulsorily insured pensioners pay 7.3% on the statutory pension plus half of the additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag), on average 1.45% in 2026. The other half is borne by the pension insurance institution. Pensioners pay the long-term care contribution of 3.6% on their own. Together that is around 12.35% of the gross pension, or around 12.95% for childless persons. Pensioners who miss the nine-tenths rule become voluntary members and, under Section 240 SGB V, pay contributions on their entire economic capacity.

bloecke.titel: Cost of the type of insurance
bloecke.md:
The assumption is €1,200 a month of capital income and rental income. For portfolio withdrawals, only the gain portion counts; the capital paid in that is withdrawn is not subject to contributions.

- Compulsory members of the KVdR pay €0 in contributions on this.
- Voluntarily insured persons pay the reduced contribution rate of 14.0% (Section 243 SGB V, without entitlement to sick pay) plus a 2.9% additional contribution plus 3.6% for long-term care, together 20.5%. That is €246 a month or €2,952 a year.

Over 25 years of retirement, this adds up to around €74,000, calculated without any contribution adjustments.

The nine-tenths rule can be influenced by the choice of health insurance, but it is assessed retrospectively for the second half of working life. Self-employed people with private health insurance and insured persons who switch to private health insurance (PKV) at 50 as a rule miss it permanently. You can check your own status in advance using the insurance history from the pension insurance and with your health insurance fund.

In private health insurance, the premium depends on the age at entry and on the state of health and not on income. It continues after the end of working life. The Association of Private Health Insurers (Verband der privaten Krankenversicherung) states an average premium for 2025 of €536 a month for adults without an entitlement to civil service healthcare allowances (Beihilfe). In the allowance tariffs (Beihilfetarife) for civil servants, it was well below €350 at all ages. In individual cases the premium is often considerably higher. The pension insurance pays a subsidy equal to half the general contribution rate and half the average additional contribution rate on the pension, that is, 8.75% in 2026, but at most half of the premium paid (Section 106(3) SGB VI, Social Code Book VI, pension insurance). A return to statutory health insurance is practically impossible from 55. To limit the premium, the remaining options are switching to another tariff with your own insurer, with the ageing reserve credited (Section 204 VVG, Insurance Contract Act), premium relief tariffs and, as a last resort, the standard or basic tariff (Standardtarif, Basistarif).

## Children's maintenance obligation

If the income of the person in need of care is not sufficient, assistance with care costs under SGB XII steps in. It is subsidiary and only applies once the income and realisable assets of the person concerned have been used. For the children, Section 94(1a) SGB XII has applied since the Relief for Relatives Act (Angehörigen-Entlastungsgesetz). Under it, the social assistance authority can only transfer maintenance claims to itself if the child's annual total income (Gesamteinkommen) within the meaning of Section 16 SGB IV (Social Code Book IV) exceeds €100,000. This is the sum of their income under income tax law, which for employees means gross wages after deducting income-related expenses (Werbungskosten), plus other income, for example from letting or capital assets. The limit applies to each child individually, and the spouse's income is not added. It is also not indexed, so with rising wages more people exceed it every year.

The €100,000 limit only protects the children's income. It does not apply to the parents' assets or to what the parents have already transferred. Under Section 528 BGB (Civil Code), an impoverished donor can reclaim the gift if they can no longer provide for their own reasonable maintenance. This claim passes to the social assistance authority. Reclaiming is only excluded ten years after the gift was made (Section 529 BGB). A transfer of the house to the children therefore above all needs time in advance. It can also come into conflict with usufruct, inheritance tax planning and the claim to supplement the compulsory share (Pflichtteilsergänzungsanspruch).

Without a [[Lasting power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht)|lasting power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht)]], nobody can dispose of the account, portfolio or ongoing contracts if care is needed. The guardianship court (Betreuungsgericht) then appoints a legal guardian, if necessary a stranger. Three points matter for the power of attorney to be usable: banks usually only accept their own forms or a notarially certified power of attorney, public certification is required for property transactions anyway (Section 29 GBO, Land Register Code), and registration in the Central Register of Lasting Powers of Attorney (Zentrales Vorsorgeregister) of the Federal Chamber of Notaries (Bundesnotarkammer) ensures that the court finds the power of attorney. The emergency right of representation between spouses (Ehegattennotvertretungsrecht) under Section 1358 BGB does not replace it, because it only applies to health matters and for a maximum of six months.

At the end of a withdrawal plan, the long-term care risk is a liquidity risk and not a return risk. It involves a need of the order of magnitude of the illustrative calculation above, that is, a gap of just over €57,000 for four years in a care home, which arises in an unknown year and has to be paid within a few years. It can be covered by a policy whose premium is still affordable at 85, by a block of assets that remains unallocated to the very end, or by a property that is sold if necessary. A withdrawal plan designed down to the last euro for regular needs does not cover this need.

mitnehmen: Because long-term care insurance only pays fixed amounts, care home residents were left with a co-payment averaging €3,677 a month nationwide on 1 July 2026, of which only the care-related part falls with the length of stay.
Four years in a care home cost around €134,000 at the national average, and whatever the pension does not cover has to come from assets, otherwise social assistance is needed.
Whether capital income and rents remain free of contributions in retirement depends on the nine-tenths prior insurance period under Section 5(1) no. 11 SGB V and not on the amount of assets.
Supplementary long-term care insurance is only useful if its premium is still affordable at 85, because on surrender everything paid in is lost.
A child is only required to pay maintenance for a parent if their total income exceeds €100,000 a year, but gifts made in the last ten years can be reclaimed regardless (Section 528 BGB).

begriffe.text: Classification from 1 to 5 based on a weighted score from six assessment modules of the Medical Service (Medizinischer Dienst). The yardstick is the remaining independence and not the diagnosis. The care level determines the amount of benefits under SGB XI.

Care-related part of the care home bill, which is the same for care levels 2 to 5 within a given home. On 1 July 2026, the national average was €2,088 a month. Only this item is reduced by the care home supplement.

Subsidy from the long-term care insurance fund under Section 43c SGB XI towards the care-related co-payment in a care home. It is graded by length of stay and amounts to 15% in the first year, 30% from the 13th month, 50% from the 25th and 75% from the 37th month.

Health insurance for pensioners (Krankenversicherung der Rentner). Compulsory membership under Section 5(1) no. 11 SGB V for pensioners who had statutory health insurance for nine tenths of the second half of their working life. Contributions are then payable only on the pension, pension-type income and earned income, not on capital income and rents.

Private supplementary insurance that pays an agreed fixed amount once a care level has been determined, regardless of the costs incurred and of where the care takes place. Without an indexation option, the benefit loses value in real terms over the term.
